cls: Inactivated viral vaccine - active immunisation against Japanese encephalitis
pharm: An inactivated, purified Japanese encephalitis virus antigen vaccine (e.g. Vero-cell-derived SA14-14-2 inactivated vaccine) that induces neutralising antibodies to prevent Japanese encephalitis
quick: 0.5 mL IM on day 0 and day 28 (two-dose primary series)
Inactivated vaccine; use only if clearly needed - data limited
Considered compatible; inactivated vaccine poses minimal risk
Immediate hypersensitivity; local and systemic reactions
summary: Inactivated Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus vaccine is a purified, inactivated whole-virus protein vaccine (such as the Vero-cell-derived SA14-14-2 inactivated vaccine, e.g. Ixiaro) used for active immunisation against Japanese encephalitis - a mosquito-borne flaviviral encephalitis endemic in much of Asia. The primary series is two intramuscular 0.5 mL doses given 28 days apart (a 0.25 mL dose is used for younger children with some products), with a booster recommended if exposure continues, typically around 1-2 years later. It is indicated for residents of and travellers to endemic areas at risk. As an inactivated vaccine it is not contraindicated by immunosuppression on theoretical grounds, although the immune response may be reduced. Reactions are usually mild and local; serious hypersensitivity is rare. This product is not represented in openFDA in this naming form; dosing follows the manufacturer's insert and WHO/ACIP recommendations.
indications: Active immunisation against Japanese encephalitis in adults and children at risk
Residents of and travellers to JE-endemic areas of Asia/Western Pacific
Laboratory workers at potential risk of exposure to JE virus

dosage.c: Adults and children (per product age cut-offs)
dosage.d: 0.5 mL on day 0 and day 28 (two-dose primary series); 0.25 mL per dose for younger children with some formulations
dosage.t: Intramuscular injection (deltoid in adults; anterolateral thigh in infants)
dosage.n: An accelerated schedule (days 0 and 7) is approved for some adult products

dosage.d: A single booster dose, typically about 1-2 years after the primary series
dosage.n: Follow the specific product insert and exposure risk

admin: Administer by intramuscular injection (deltoid in adults/older children; anterolateral thigh in infants); do not give intravenously
Shake well before use if a suspension; inspect for particulates/discoloration and discard if present
Complete the two-dose primary series ideally at least 1 week before potential exposure
Do not mix with other vaccines in the same syringe; use separate sites if co-administering
Have adrenaline and resuscitation facilities available; observe after injection
Store and transport at 2-8 C and do not freeze
moa: The inactivated Japanese encephalitis virus antigen is presented to the immune system without the capacity to replicate, stimulating production of JE-virus-specific neutralising antibodies and immune memory. These neutralising antibodies prevent infection of host cells by wild-type JE virus on subsequent exposure, conferring active protective immunity against Japanese encephalitis. Because the virus is inactivated, immunity develops without risk of vaccine-derived JE disease.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity to a previous dose or to any vaccine component (e.g. protamine sulfate in certain products)
Acute severe febrile illness (defer until recovery)
relative: Pregnancy (limited data; use only if clearly needed)

preg: There are limited data on the use of inactivated JE vaccine in pregnancy. As an inactivated vaccine the theoretical risk is low, but it should generally be used during pregnancy only if the risk of JE exposure is substantial and clearly outweighs any potential risk. Where possible, defer travel to endemic areas rather than vaccinate.
lact: Inactivated JE vaccine is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding, as inactivated vaccines pose minimal theoretical risk to the breastfed infant. Vaccinate if the mother is at risk of exposure.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy - may reduce the antibody response to the vaccine
Other vaccines - can generally be co-administered at separate sites
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently affect flavivirus serology interpretation

common: Injection-site pain, redness, swelling or induration
rare: Neurological events (very rare and not clearly causally linked for modern inactivated vaccines)
emergency: Anaphylaxis with airway compromise or shock

monitoring: Observation for immediate hypersensitivity for about 15-30 minutes after each dose
Completion of the two-dose primary series and any booster
counsel: This vaccine protects against Japanese encephalitis, a brain infection spread by mosquito bites in parts of Asia
You need two doses (usually 28 days apart) to be fully protected - complete the course before travel/exposure
Mild arm soreness, headache or tiredness is common and short-lived
Continue to avoid mosquito bites (repellents, nets, covering up) - no vaccine is 100% protective
Tell the clinic if you are pregnant or have had a serious reaction to a previous dose
Seek urgent help for any rash, facial/throat swelling or breathing difficulty after vaccination
pk: Protective antibodies develop after completing the two-dose primary series (around 1 week after the second dose)
Peak neutralising antibody titres a few weeks after the second dose
Not applicable - vaccine induces active immunity rather than measurable drug levels
Protection for at least 1-2 years; a booster extends immunity for continued risk
Store at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: Primary series is two IM doses 28 days apart (an accelerated days 0/7 schedule exists for some adult products); booster around 1-2 years for ongoing risk
Inactivated vaccine - lower theoretical risk than live vaccines, but response may be blunted by immunosuppression
Indicated for travellers to and residents of JE-endemic areas; complete before exposure
Vaccination supplements, not replaces, mosquito-bite avoidance
Not represented in openFDA under this name - dosing follows the manufacturer's insert and WHO/ACIP guidance
missed: If the second dose of the primary series is delayed, give it as soon as possible - the series does not need to be restarted. For a missed booster, administer it when convenient based on ongoing exposure risk and the product schedule.
overdose: Overdose is very unlikely with single-dose presentations. Inadvertent administration of an excess dose is managed with observation and supportive care; no specific antidote is needed.
